findings.title: OS Command Injection via Filename
findings.trigger: If the filename is controlled by an attacker, they could inject a malicious filename that leads to OS command execution.
findings.assumptions: The `readFileIntoRawString` function directly uses the filename to open a file, and there is no validation or sanitization of the filename.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via Filename
findings.trigger: If the filename is controlled by an attacker, they could inject a malicious filename that leads to OS command execution.
findings.assumptions: The `writeToTxtFile` function directly uses the filename to open a file for writing, and there is no validation or sanitization of the filename.

findings.title: Uncontrolled Search Path Element
findings.trigger: If the categories list is dynamically populated from untrusted input, an attacker could inject a malicious category that leads to arbitrary file access.
findings.assumptions: The `removeLineStartingWith` function removes lines starting with a specific sequence, and the categories list is populated from untrusted input.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via Filename
findings.trigger: If the output string is controlled by an attacker, they could inject a malicious filename that leads to OS command execution.
findings.assumptions: The `writeToTxtFile` function directly uses the filename to open a file for writing, and there is no validation or sanitization of the filename.
